name: Visual Journal
tagline: One art director's blog of branding and graphic design, selected by personal research and a stated reductive, modernist eye
description:
Visual Journal is Alessandro Scarpellini's blog. He is an art director and design manager in Italy, and he describes his own visual language as reductive and modernist, working in strategy, branding and visual communication.

That declared position is the reason to read it. Most galleries hide their taste behind a submission queue. This one names the eye doing the selecting, so the collection is coherent and you know what it is coherent about.

The subject is branding and graphic design rather than interfaces: identity work, editorial design and visual communication, chosen through what he calls careful, personal research.

Submissions go by email, and he asks for a complete case study in a Drive or Dropbox folder organised into two sections. That is a higher bar than a form, and it explains why the collection stays small and consistent.

The site is a client-rendered shell of about 8.7 KB. It publishes no llms.txt and no sitemap.
pricing_detail: Free to read, with no account. The site asks for support and takes submissions by email.
agent_guidance:
Reach for it for identity and editorial work, not for interfaces. The subject is branding and graphic design, so it answers a different brief from the site galleries in this corpus.

Read the stated position before you use it. He names his language as reductive and modernist, so the collection argues for one aesthetic rather than covering the field.

Send a person. The page is an 8.7 KB client-rendered shell with no llms.txt, no sitemap and no per-project route in the served HTML, so an agent cannot walk the projects.
why_it_matters: A gallery that names its curator and their aesthetic is a stronger reference than one that hides behind a submission form, because you can judge the selection against a stated position.
tier_reason: Named curation with a declared aesthetic and a demanding submission standard, covering branding and editorial work that the interface galleries here do not. Held at C because nothing is machine-readable: an 8.7 KB shell, no llms.txt, no sitemap, no published total and no per-project route a fetch can reach.
